rationale: Psalm 43 says all-day humiliation is before the speaker and the shame of his face covered him. Psalm 68 says embarrassment covered his face after endured reproach. Both express disgrace as a covering, while the source's shame-of-the-face covering the speaker is not rewritten as the target's covering of the face.

Psalm 50 appeals to divine mercy and compassion for the blotting out of his lawless deed. Isaiah presents God as the One who wipes out lawless acts and will not remember. The erasure of wrongdoing corresponds as requested mercy and divine declaration.
